solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lots of money but not much luck

explanation.surface: A gambler wins plenty of cash yet feels their luck is thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' only links the definition to the wordplay, and the phrase is ironic: a 'small' fortune is really a large one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom ironically names a very large sum, as in costing a fortune.

clue.text: Spoil vote? It's unusual for a left-winger

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of the word before are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone spoiling a ballot paper would be odd behaviour for a committed socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Karl Marx's communism sits on the political left.

clue.text: Butcher's first to go, causing tears — on the contrary!

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for butcher is dropped, as the clue says goes

explanation.surface: A butcher's work makes people weep, the clue claims, then flips it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to go' removes the S of SLAUGHTER. Slaughter causes tears of grief; 'on the contrary' turns this to the merriment that brings tears of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty mirth can make the eyes stream, so it brings on tears of the happy kind.

clue.text: Swift starts to fly after seeing them

indicators.note: the starts of the four following words supply their opening letters

explanation.surface: Birds called swifts begin to fly once they have spotted something.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift and quick are plain synonyms for moving at speed.

clue.text: Satirical plays on society expose these bigots

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters of satirical being played around with

explanation.surface: Satires about society unmask prejudiced people.
explanation.definitionFit: Those prejudiced against other races are a kind of intolerant people.

clue.text: Single French one goes over mid-week

indicators.note: in a down light the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Wednesday, abbreviated Wed, is the middle of the week

explanation.surface: A lone French person travels across in the middle of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Single in the marital sense means not having married.

clue.text: Mine's found in an untidy heap with an inscription

indicators.note: found in places one piece within the other
an untidy heap has its letters in disorder

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Someone claims their property turned up in a messy pile with writing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine's' reads as a possessive, but it is the noun mine, a coal pit; 'untidy' rearranges heap around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Words carved on a gravestone are a memorial inscription.

clue.text: Lead for building material — steel's better for this

parts.note: a rein is a lead for a horse

explanation.surface: Builders debate metal against steel when strengthening a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal, in contrast to steel, but it is the strap that guides a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel bars strengthen concrete, and that strengthening is what the clue's last words describe.

clue.text: Troublesome types who would challenge a beautician

definitions.text: Troublesome types who would challenge a beautician

parts.words: Troublesome types who would challenge a beautician
parts.note: unpleasant people are called this idiomatically, and plain-looking clients would test a beautician's skill

explanation.surface: Awkward clients give a beauty salon a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for nasty, menacing people, read literally, means unattractive clients of a salon.

clue.text: Don't start crying, son, they're meant to tell you off

definitions.text: they're meant to tell you off

indicators.note: the word for crying must not begin with its first letter

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent urges a boy not to cry, as the scolding is for his own good.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a stern lecture is informally receiving a long scolding.

clue.text: Engine cover and clutch contain rotating tungsten ring

indicators.note: contain puts the next pieces inside the word for clutch
rotating turns the two letters round

parts.note: W is the chemical symbol for tungsten

explanation.surface: A mechanic lists car parts: bonnet, clutch and a spinning metal ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The removable metal casing over an aircraft engine is its streamlined housing.

clue.text: Name and number mostly coming from the horse's mouth

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A racing tip gives a name and number, straight from the horse's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A whinny is the cry a horse makes, so it literally comes out of its mouth.

clue.text: Fifty-plus male seen with unknown woman of property

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An older man is spotted out with a mysterious wealthy woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who owns and lets a house is its proprietress.

clue.text: Dressing that's 50% slimming and 50% definitely not!

definitions.text: Dressing that's 50% slimming and 50% definitely not!

parts.words: Dressing that's 50% slimming and 50% definitely not!
parts.note: a bottled condiment whose first word is diet food and whose second is fattening

explanation.surface: A dieter notes that a condiment is half healthy and half anything but.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottled British condiment is a mayonnaise-like topping for leaves.

clue.text: Why Etonian could be making an entry

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters given might become something else rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a pupil of Eton might be arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone arriving is coming through the door, an idiom for entering.

clue.text: You used to be grand

definitions.meaning: the old form of the second-person pronoun
slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone tells another they were once magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the archaic 'you', and also short for thousand, which slang calls a grand.

clue.text: Over-stuff one to make a spicy sandwich filling

parts.note: to ram is to stuff something in
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Overfilling something to make a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned smoked beef is a spiced deli meat sliced into sandwiches.

clue.text: Carbon copy for the head

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A carbon copy is made for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland jutting into the sea, not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland projecting into the sea is a promontory.

clue.text: Two royals perhaps need a second to make a third

definitions.text: Two royals perhaps need a second to make a third

parts.words: Two royals perhaps need a second to make a third
parts.note: a pair of king's sons, given another S, turns into a king's daughter

explanation.surface: A riddle about royal arithmetic: two members plus a second make a third.
explanation.walkthrough: Add a second S to the plural of prince and you get PRINCESS, a third kind of royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Two sons of a monarch are a pair of royal heirs.

clue.text: Dan at No 10 is a master of one

definitions.text: Dan at No 10 is a master of one

parts.words: Dan at No 10 is a master of one
parts.note: the tenth dan is a top grade in judo or karate, held by a master of such a discipline

explanation.surface: Someone named Dan living at Downing Street is an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 suggests Downing Street, the Prime Minister's address, but a dan is a black-belt grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo and karate are fighting disciplines ranked by dans.

clue.text: Eastern triads travelling on horseback

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters moving about

explanation.surface: Asian gangs journey on horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits with a leg on each side of the saddle, legs apart.

clue.text: Dine out in a raincoat here on board

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a mack is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

indicators.note: out signals the word dine being rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat outdoors wearing a waterproof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges dine; 'in' sets those letters within the raincoat, spelt as the short form of mackintosh.
explanation.definitionFit: On board a ship, the principal deck running stem to stern is where the clue says.

clue.text: It means the same party adopts it on time

indicators.note: adopts means the word for party takes the other pieces in

explanation.surface: A political party sticks to the same line, adopting it punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: The word used to say 'likewise' marks a repetition of what came before.

clue.text: Such Poles used to build Shinto temples

indicators.note: the letters of the next words are used, run together, to build the answer

explanation.surface: Wooden poles were used in the construction of Japanese shrines.
explanation.definitionFit: Carved posts bearing tribal emblems are the poles in question.

clue.text: With it a bird lacks perception

indicators.note: lacks means the word for bird is without the next piece

explanation.surface: A trendy bird is said to be lacking in insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stylish and fashionable is being with it.

clue.text: Brass fastener not required with t-shirt

parts.note: brass neck is British slang for cheek or nerve, so brass gives neck

explanation.surface: No brass buttons or fasteners needed when wearing a t-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A collar-and-cravat accessory is out of place with a casual top.

clue.text: Find out about rival having put on weight

indicators.note: about wraps the word for find out round the next piece

parts.note: to hear is to find out

explanation.surface: Discovering a competitor has gained a few pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has gained weight is now of greater mass.

clue.text: Cash lost in 'em is extraordinary

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters being made into something out of the ordinary

explanation.surface: The amount of money gamblers lose in fruit machines is staggering.
explanation.definitionFit: Coin-operated gambling machines swallow players' money.
